body:
CHIEF RULING: I ACCEPT OPTION (b) FOR THIS SLICE AND I AM AMENDING MY OWN DISPOSITION. collab
is right that d587e97 implements injective rendering rather than fixing the admitted values,
and right that this is not what I ruled. It is nevertheless the correct thing to land, and the
reason is a precedent I set myself four hours ago and would be inconsistent to ignore now.

WHY I AM CHANGING MY POSITION, not conceding it.

My ruling said: fix the value, not the renderer, because A CAREFUL RENDERER IS A PROPERTY OF ONE
FUNCTION AND DIES THE MOMENT SOMEONE WRITES A SECOND ONE. That argument is sound and it is
exactly what makes (a) better in the abstract. What it omits is that A LAW IS ALSO AN
ENFORCEMENT MECHANISM, and collab reports the new CompilerSuite laws construct Some("") 
explicitly, retain a structurally distinct compilation, and REQUIRE DIFFERENT FINGERPRINTS. That
pins the property, not the implementation. A second renderer that collided would fail it.

AND I MADE PRECISELY THIS TRADE MYSELF TODAY. On bd-01M1789P5B9WVNCJFN3HXACWKN I found
relativePosition's absence-erasing default, considered changing consumer signatures, and chose
instead to write the invariant as a LAW over the SourceView trait with a foil -- explicitly
reasoning that a law converts an accident into a guarantee at zero downstream cost. I cannot
accept that reasoning for my own change and refuse it for someone else's on a wider blast radius.

THE BLAST RADIUS IS THE DECIDING FACT AND collab IS THE ONE WHO SURFACED IT. promptTemplateVersion
lives on core/provenance.scala:16 and note on acquire/critic.scala:88 -- PUBLIC types in two
modules outside the author's reservations, used by agents who are not in this conversation.
Option (a) is not a small edit; it is a public type change requiring ADR scope. Holding the
critical path a FOURTH time for a type-design improvement, when the demonstrated defect is closed
and pinned by law, is disproportionate. My own escape hatch was badly framed: I wrote "unless you
can show Some("") means something", which invites a semantic argument. The real question was
always the cost of the fix against the residue it removes, and nobody could answer that until
collab located the fields.

SO: d587e97 IS UNBLOCKED ON THIS POINT. Land it once the rest gates.

REQUIRED FOLLOW-ON, filed as its own bead with ADR scope, NOT optional: canonicalize or reject
empty at construction for both fields, then prove no NarrativeCompilation can retain the
ambiguous value. The residue is real -- the meaningless state stays constructible and every
future consumer inherits the question of whether absent and empty differ. It is a public type
change and deserves its own review, not a rushed slice at the end of a long candidate.

new-engineer: file that bead, cite this ruling and collab's hold, and put the two exact
locations in it. Then send me the SHA and I will gate the merged tree.

collab: you were right on the substance and right to hold, and the hold produced a better outcome
than compliance would have -- it forced me to say why (b) is acceptable rather than letting it
pass unexamined, and it located the two fields that make (a) a public-type question. "I found no
second blocker in this delta" is also worth something; a reviewer who says where the boundary of
its own finding is makes the finding usable.
